h1: The 6 Best Printers for Remote Workers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Printers for Remote Workers: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six home-office printers for remote workers compared on laser vs ink, scan and fax, running cost and footprint.
summary: The Brother DCP-L2640DW is the best printer for steady daily work, a compact laser with duplex, copy and scan. The HP OfficeJet Pro 8139 handles scan, fax and a document feeder. Color users should look at the Epson EcoTank ET-2800, and text-only users at the Brother HL-L2405W.
intro: Remote workers usually buy the wrong printer for how often they print. A home inkjet that sits idle for weeks clogs its heads, while a laser keeps its toner dry indefinitely. Match the technology to your habit before you look at features.
We reviewed eight wireless printers and ranked six on print type, office functions, ink or toner cost and desk footprint. Rankings come from the spec sheets, not print tests.

products.name: Brother DCP-L2640DW Wireless Compact Monochrome Laser Printer
products.verdict: The lowest running cost for daily work, with copy and scan.
products.description:
The DCP-L2640DW is a wireless compact monochrome laser with duplex printing, copy and scan. It works with Alexa, supports mobile printing and includes a Refresh subscription trial. It sits in the $200 to $500 band.

It ranks first because toner lasts far longer than ink for steady daily printing. It ranks above the HL-L2405W since it adds a scanner and copier for a higher cost.

It suits remote workers who print invoices and contracts daily. It prints in black and white only.

products.name: HP OfficeJet Pro 8139 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: Print, scan, copy and fax with a document feeder.
products.description:
The OfficeJet Pro 8139 is a wireless color inkjet all-in-one with print, scan, copy and fax, an auto document feeder, duplex and a 1-year Instant Ink trial. Expect to pay in the $100 to $200 range.

It ranks second since it is the only pick with an auto document feeder and fax, but ink costs more over time than laser toner.

It suits workers who scan multipage contracts. If you print rarely, ink may dry out.
products.skipIf: You print only a few pages a month.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-2800 Wireless Color All-in-One Supertank Printer
products.verdict: Color printing from refillable ink tanks, with no cartridges.
products.description:
The ET-2800 is a wireless color all-in-one with cartridge-free refillable ink tanks, and it prints, scans and copies. Expect to pay in the $100 to $200 range.

It ranks third because tanks lower ink cost for occasional color but the body is larger than a compact laser. It sits above the ET-2400 for a more complete feature set.

It suits workers who print color presentations now and then. Leave desk space for the tanks.

products.name: Brother HL-L2405W Wireless Compact Monochrome Laser Printer
products.verdict: A simple laser for printing text and nothing else.
products.description:
The HL-L2405W is a wireless compact monochrome laser with mobile printing, Alexa support and a Refresh subscription trial. Expect to pay in the $100 to $200 range.

It ranks below the DCP-L2640DW because it has no scanner or copier, but it costs a band less.

It suits workers who only print. If you ever scan receipts, pick the DCP or an all-in-one.

products.name: Epson Workforce WF-2930 Wireless All-in-One Printer
products.verdict: Scan, copy and fax with a feeder at a low price.
products.description:
The WF-2930 is a wireless all-in-one inkjet with print, scan, copy and fax, an auto document feeder, duplex and a 1.4 inch color display. Street cost lands in the $50 to $100 range.

Fifth place reflects the fact that cartridge ink costs more over time than the EcoTank models. It does give you a feeder and fax in the lowest band.

It suits budget buyers who need office functions. Heavy printers should consider tanks.

products.name: HP Smart Tank 5101 Wireless All-in-One Refillable Printer
products.verdict: Two years of ink included, but 2.4GHz Wi-Fi only.
products.description:
The Smart Tank 5101 is a wireless refillable all-in-one with print, scan and copy, and it includes two years of ink. Expect to pay in the $100 to $200 range.

It ranks last because it supports 2.4GHz wireless only, which can be a problem on modern 5GHz-only networks.

It suits workers who want to forget about ink for two years. Check your router first.

methodology.title: Print technology
methodology.description: Laser versus inkjet versus tank was compared against how often a remote worker prints.

methodology.title: Office functions
methodology.description: Scan, copy, fax and auto document feeders were weighed for home-office usefulness.

methodology.title: Running cost
methodology.description: Toner, cartridges, tanks and included ink were compared as ongoing costs.

methodology.title: Footprint
methodology.description: Compact bodies scored higher for small desks.

methodology.title: Connectivity
methodology.description: Wireless, mobile printing and voice assistant support earned credit.

whatMatters.detail: Lasers use dry toner that never clogs and suit steady document printing. Inkjets print color but can dry out if unused. Match the type to how often you print. Look for monochrome laser in the title.
The cheap printer is not the cheap printing. Tank printers carry large ink reservoirs that lower per-page cost. Toner lasts for many pages. Check what is included in the box.
A flatbed scanner handles single pages, while a feeder handles multipage contracts. Remote workers who sign documents benefit from a feeder. Look for ADF in the specs.
Some printers only join 2.4GHz networks. Routers set to 5GHz only will not see them. Confirm the band before buying.
Tank printers are larger because of the ink tanks. A compact laser fits a shelf. Measure the space first.

faq.q: Can these print from my phone?
faq.a: The Brother models list mobile printing support. Most wireless printers here also work with phone apps.
Cartridges are costly per page. The WF-2930 is a budget exception for light users.

faq.q: Is the HP Smart Tank 5101 compatible with my router?
faq.a: It supports 2.4GHz wireless only, so a 5GHz-only router will not work.

faq.q: How do I set up wirelessly?
faq.a: Use the maker's app, join your Wi-Fi network and install the driver on your computer.

faq.q: How do I prevent clogged ink?
faq.a: Print a page weekly. Lasers like the Brother DCP-L2640DW do not clog.
Few remote workers do. The HP 8139 and Epson WF-2930 are the picks that include it.

finalTake: The Brother DCP-L2640DW is the best printer for most remote workers, thanks to laser economy with copy and scan. Choose the HP OfficeJet Pro 8139 if you scan stacks of pages, and the Epson EcoTank ET-2800 for occasional color. The WF-2930 is the budget route.
